question: Compare the disclosed financing profiles of AGEL and APSEZ on debt maturity structure, interest-rate exposure and reliance on related-party or promoter funding, and say which shows more refinancing risk on the disclosed evidence.
scope: First-pass comparison of the disclosed financing profiles of Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL, FY25 annual report excerpts) and Adani Ports & SEZ Ltd (APSEZ, Q1 FY27 excerpts) across three dimensions: debt maturity structure, interest-rate exposure, and reliance on related-party/promoter funding. Both the credit and compliance specialists returned INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE for a like-for-like comparison: AGEL disclosures are detailed on all three dimensions, while the APSEZ excerpts contain only covenant/ratio formulae, NCD covenant terms and a security-cover certificate table. No comparative refinancing-risk conclusion is drawn here, and no rating, score or outlook is assigned.

key_findings.text: AGEL consolidated contractual maturities of borrowings (including current maturities and interest accrued) at March 31, 2025: <1 year ₹16,991 crore; 1-5 years ₹53,684 crore; >5 years ₹60,037 crore; total ₹1,30,712 crore. Prior year (March 31, 2024): ₹28,004 crore / ₹38,012 crore / ₹48,738 crore; total ₹1,14,754 crore — i.e. a larger total book with a materially smaller sub-1-year bucket year on year.

AGEL standalone contractual maturities of borrowings including trade credits from banks (including current maturities and interest accrued) at March 31, 2025: <1 year ₹8,280 crore; 1-5 years ₹14,493 crore; nil shown beyond 5 years; total ₹22,773 crore. The standalone disclosure also references footnotes on extension of loan tenure payable in the current and next year.

AGEL discloses explicit reliance on related-party support for repayment flexibility: at consolidated level 'the Group also has support from related parties to extend repayment terms of borrowings due to them, as needed'; at standalone level the same support is stated in respect of inter-corporate borrowings due to subsidiaries. AGEL also states it monitors funding and refinancing options in debt and capital markets and has access to debt-market instruments.

A specific instance of related-party funding reliance is disclosed: unsecured inter-corporate deposits from related parties bearing interest of 10.60%-11.00% p.a.; the tenure of an ICD balance of ₹751 crore originally payable in January 2026 and March 2026 was extended by 3 years (further extendable by 2 years by mutual agreement) effective March 1, 2025.

AGEL current borrowings detail: current maturities of non-current borrowings of ₹3,826 crore at March 31, 2025 versus ₹17,611 crore at March 31, 2024; secured working capital loans from banks of ₹1,216 crore (prior year ₹612 crore) at 7.75%-8.00% p.a., repayable as a bullet at the end of 6 months from disbursement, alongside trade credit from banks.

AGEL interest-rate exposure: exposure relates to floating-rate term loans from banks/financial institutions, which existed in the prior year; for the current year AGEL states there is no interest rate risk because borrowings are mostly at fixed rates of interest.
AGEL disclosed a bond issuance secured by charges over operating project cash flows and reserve accounts at a fixed 4.375% p.a., fully repaid during the year on September 8, 2024.

For APSEZ, the only debt-specific covenant disclosure is for one 2016 NCD tranche (ISIN INE742F07361, ₹252 crore) with financial covenants of DSCR > 1.10x and Net Gearing (Total Net Debt/Tangible Net Worth) < 3x; no maturity schedule, interest-rate exposure or related-party/promoter funding reliance is disclosed for this or other APSEZ debt in the excerpts.

The APSEZ security-cover certificate is the only quantitative debt disclosure in the excerpts and does not break down maturity timing, fixed/floating structure or related-party funding sources. Specialists report the figures differently: the credit specialist cites listed secured NCD book value of ₹10,275.10 crore plus other secured/unsecured borrowings of ₹35,608.46 crore with associated asset coverage; the compliance specialist cites the same ₹10,275.10 crore NCD book value against total liabilities of ₹45,171.29 crore and additionally characterises the table as having largely blank/illegible figures. This divergence in how the table is read is not resolved on the evidence provided.

The remaining APSEZ material consists of ratio definitions only — formulae for Debt Equity Ratio, Debt Service Coverage Ratio, Interest Service Coverage Ratio and Long Term Debt to Working Capital Ratio — without computed values, so none of the three comparison dimensions can be populated for APSEZ.

Both specialists conclude that the evidence does not permit a determination of which entity carries more refinancing risk: AGEL's refinancing-risk indicators (near-term and medium-term maturity buckets, documented related-party dependency and negotiated extensions) are disclosed, while APSEZ's equivalent indicators are absent from the excerpts. The asymmetry reflects disclosure coverage in the excerpts, not a demonstrated difference in underlying risk.

claims.text: AGEL's consolidated contractual maturity of borrowings (including current maturities and interest accrued) was: less than 1 year ₹16,991 crore, 1-5 years ₹53,684 crore, more than 5 years ₹60,037 crore, total ₹1,30,712 crore as at March 31, 2025; compared to less than 1 year ₹28,004 crore, 1-5 years ₹38,012 crore, more than 5 years ₹48,738 crore, total ₹1,14,754 crore as at March 31, 2024.

At the standalone (AGEL company) level, contractual maturities of borrowings including trade credits from banks (including current maturities and interest accrued) were: less than 1 year ₹8,280 crore, 1-5 years ₹14,493 crore, more than 5 years ₹0, total ₹22,773 crore as at March 31, 2025.

AGEL states it consistently monitors funding and refinancing options in debt and capital markets, and discloses that 'the Group also has support from related parties to extend repayment terms of borrowings due to them, as needed' (consolidated) and that 'the Company also has support from related parties (subsidiaries) to extend repayment terms of inter corporate borrowings due to them, as needed' (standalone).

AGEL discloses a specific instance of related-party (promoter-group inter-corporate deposit) funding reliance: unsecured ICDs from related parties carrying interest of 10.60%-11.00% p.a.; the tenure of an ICD balance of ₹751 crore, originally payable in January 2026 and March 2026, was extended for a further 3 years (further extendable by 2 years by mutual agreement) effective March 1, 2025.

AGEL's current borrowings included 'Current maturities of Non current borrowings' of ₹3,826 crore as at March 31, 2025, down from ₹17,611 crore as at March 31, 2024, alongside working capital loans from banks carrying interest of 7.75%-8.00% p.a.

AGEL discloses that its interest-rate risk relates to floating-rate term loans from banks/financial institutions; in the prior year there was such exposure, but 'there is no interest rate risk during the current year, considering Company's borrowings in current year are mostly at fixed rate of interest.'

AGEL also disclosed a bond issuance secured by charges over operating project cash flows and reserve accounts carrying a fixed interest rate of 4.375% p.a., which was fully repaid during the year (repaid September 8, 2024).

For APSEZ, the only debt-related covenant information disclosed is for one 2016 NCD tranche (ISIN INE742F07361, ₹252 crore), with financial covenants of DSCR > 1.10x and Net Gearing (Total Net Debt/Tangible Net Worth) < 3x; no maturity schedule, interest-rate exposure, or related-party/promoter funding reliance is disclosed for this or other APSEZ debt in the excerpts.

APSEZ's security cover certificate shows book values of listed secured non-convertible debentures (₹10,275.10 crore) and other secured/unsecured borrowings (₹35,608.46 crore) with associated asset coverage, but provides no breakdown of maturity timing (short-term vs long-term), interest-rate structure, or related-party funding sources.

On the evidence disclosed, AGEL explicitly documents reliance on related-party/promoter funding with negotiated extensions of repayment terms on inter-corporate deposits and borrowings, together with a detailed maturity ladder showing substantial near-term (under 1 year) and medium-term (1-5 year) borrowings; APSEZ's excerpts do not contain comparable maturity-ladder, interest-rate-exposure, or related-party-funding disclosures, so the evidence does not permit a definitive comparative conclusion on which entity carries more refinancing risk overall — it only supports that AGEL's disclosed refinancing-risk indicators (related-party dependency, near-term maturities) are documented, while APSEZ's equivalent indicators are not present in the provided excerpts.

by_specialist.note: The excerpts provide detailed debt maturity, interest-rate and related-party funding disclosures for AGEL (both consolidated and standalone) but do not contain comparable disclosures for APSEZ. The APSEZ excerpts consist only of ratio/covenant formula definitions, a security-cover certificate table for listed NCDs, and financial covenant terms (DSCR, Net Gearing) for one 2016 NCD tranche — they do not disclose a maturity ladder, interest-rate risk exposure, or any reliance on related-party/promoter funding for APSEZ. APSEZ's standalone security cover table shows a total secured Non-Convertible Debenture book value of \u20b910,275.10 crore against total liabilities of \u20b945,171.29 crore, but the table does not break down maturity timing, interest rate type, or related-party/promoter funding sources, so it cannot be used to assess refinancing risk relative to AGEL.
